additions.context_text: The recovered reports make the transition from browsing to querying more explicit. Smeagol lets users navigate concrete resources, select a subgraph and generalize nodes into variables; RDF Explorer combines pattern construction with constant-to-variable generalization and current-result feedback. The DBpedia Visualizer applies related operations through Android gestures, while KGVis allows transformations between query patterns and result graphs \citep{V3-02525,V3-02210,V3-00229,V3-01622}. The reusable state is therefore more than a displayed neighborhood: it includes which nodes are constants, which are variables and which edges constrain the answer. The DBpedia report describes filters, aggregates and autocomplete as future work, so the gesture-based workflow does not establish the expressiveness of a full SPARQL editor.

additions.context_text: A similar-looking graph can represent different objects at successive stages. The visual data-schema library contracts classes and properties to produce configurable UML-like source-schema diagrams; initiating queries directly from those diagrams is future work. Schema-based ViziQuer uses a class tree to start queries, and the Wikidata extension displays a query pattern with readable entity labels and reverse SPARQL visualization \citep{V3-00138,V3-02393,V3-02757}. KG3D, in contrast, uses a three-dimensional entity view alongside query construction and tabular answers \citep{V3-01616}. Schema simplification, query notation and result exploration require separate representation roles even when they use nodes and links. Lossy schema abstraction also needs an explicit indication of what the view omits.

additions.context_text: Query-by-example is not one uniform interaction. The GF framework uses a grid of classes, properties, conditions and selected output fields. CUTE accepts tabular example tuples; iQbees starts from an entity and updates semantic-aspect rankings through positive and negative feedback. SPARQL-QBE builds conjunctive constraints from positive and negative entities, while Von-QBE maps keyword input through an ontology schema and suggests fragment expansions \citep{V3-00165,V3-00742,V3-01566,V3-02185,V3-02018}. These mechanisms differ in whether an example specifies a table row, an entity, a graph fragment or a conceptual starting point. Their expressive limits and feedback semantics should be stated before treating the shared name as evidence of equivalent user control.

additions.context_text: Views can also reorganize relationships without changing their role into source assertions. LDViz connects editable SPARQL queries and style sheets with coordinated MGExplorer views and exploration history. ARViz synchronizes scatter, chord and association-graph views of mined rules and provides links to the supporting publications \citep{V3-01178,V3-00411}. Stunning Doodle places embedding neighbors beside asserted knowledge-graph links, with distance-based shading and a neighbor list \citep{V3-02586}. These examples support preserving the distinction between returned facts, mined associations and embedding similarity throughout selection, explanation and export. Sparklis nested tables address a different presentation problem by using query-variable dependencies to group results and reduce repeated values; no measured usability gain is supplied for that extension \citep{V3-00261}.

additions.context_text: Guidance can reduce the visible choices while introducing a risk of losing the desired target. SView ranks link patterns by goodness and diversity and exposes hierarchy, list and top-$k$ organizations. Its user comparison found shorter interactions with top-$k$ patterns, but twelve of the twenty-four participants noted target-loss risk; hierarchy improved overview while deep branches confused some participants \citep{V3-01744}. RelClus instead groups relationship paths into a labeled hierarchy, with expansion and collapse for inspecting the grouped results \citep{V3-02740}. Ranked pruning and grouped overview support different actions. A system that reduces options should retain a route back to the full candidate set and distinguish an absent target from one hidden by ranking.

additions.context_text: An implemented host interface does not make every guidance extension implemented. The OptiqueVQS query-history report specifies conditional-probability ranking of continuations through partial-query matching, illustrated with an assumed query log; the ranking is a proposed method. A later query-log report combines proposed ranking and dead-end approximation, reporting a preliminary elimination of up to 80\% of dead ends using views about 10\% of the original data \citep{V3-02739,V3-01984}. Combined ranking and dead-end evaluation remains future work. Separately, OWL graph projection supplies a concrete navigation component used in OptiqueVQS and SemFacet, while summarizing earlier application evaluations rather than recruiting a new cohort \citep{V3-01948}. These reports warrant separate method, implementation and study identities within the same family.

additions.context_text: Conversational exploration also depends on a declared interaction scope. The news agent of Schneider et al. uses a Neo4j graph and structured exploration modes, with suggestions for related entities; unrestricted language-model generation is future work. Its 54 users produced 65 sessions, with mean SUS 79.4 (SD 18.5), but only 130 of 222 entity-related search requests were recognized \citep{V3-01173}. Seabra et al. implement clarification and reformulation with a knowledge graph and GPT-4o, illustrated through four underspecified questions about historical Brazilian capitals; quantitative participant evaluation remains future work \citep{V3-01170}. User ratings in the former and clarification examples in the latter provide different evidence. Neither establishes arbitrary conversational access across graphs or reliable resolution of every ambiguous question.

additions.context_text: Preferences can affect filtering, ordering and subsequent recommendations in different ways. PFSgeo combines facets with rectangular geographic selection and best/worst preference actions; one geographical facet is implemented. SEED V3 applies weighted positive and negative entity/aspect feedback and provides graph-link explanations of embedding-ranked entities \citep{V3-02091,V3-02418}. LINDASearch records preference learning and query recommendations, but its three-expert assessment concerns analytic annotation choices rather than a three-person end-to-end search trial \citep{V3-01754}. An application should distinguish a hard restriction from a soft preference and retain the feedback history that changes a ranked result. A related graph path explains a connection without proving that an embedding score itself is a source assertion.

additions.context_text: The recovered sources expose distinct portability costs. Humboldt works with locally loaded RDF documents and SPARQL; run-time dereferencing remains a planned extension. FedViz uses dataset class/property connectivity to build and execute federated queries, whereas the KeyFS/MidSemI architecture aligns enterprise SQL, Facebook JSON and a DBpedia RDF dump through explicit mapping components \citep{V3-01337,V3-01125,V3-01741}. Graph projection translates OWL axioms into navigable structures for existing query interfaces \citep{V3-01948}. These are different access and schema-maintenance arrangements. Their data routes must be recorded directly rather than inferred from a graph-shaped view or a list of backend engine names.

additions.context_text: Source size and interactive cost remain separate in the extension. LDViz describes a DBpedia source of about 400 million triples, while its illustrated visual graphs have 26 nodes/124 links and 237 nodes/1,160 links \citep{V3-01709,V3-01178}. additions.context_text: Measured scalability can depend sharply on the action and cache state. SPARQL-QBE reports average query execution of 103 milliseconds on its approximately one-million-triple movie dataset; feedback ranking initially ranges from 103 to 824 milliseconds and is about 103 milliseconds when cached. These are client-component times on the specified browser and hardware \citep{V3-02185}. PFSgeo separately tests synthetic datasets up to 20,000 hotels: average initialization is 1.8 seconds, yet some large-data preference actions exceed 100 seconds and the per-object alternative times out \citep{V3-02091}. Its human trial uses only twenty hotels. Reporting an initialization average or a warm-cache result as a uniform interaction bound would conceal a material workload difference.

RDF Explorer compares query construction with Wikidata Query Helper in a within-subject study of 28 fourth-year computer-science students without prior SPARQL knowledge. additions.context_text: Offline guidance tests answer different questions from human trials. iQbees evaluates 163 INEX topics with simulated feedback: positive and mixed feedback improve its ranking, while a single negative hint does not. Von-QBE evaluates selected IMDB and QALD queries without recruiting users; reported precision is 0.69 for IMDB and 0.0047 for the QALD subset \citep{V3-01566,V3-02018}. The ViziQuer Wikidata demonstration successfully visualizes 105 of 120 example queries under a criterion combining returned-result agreement with mathematical equivalence for timeout or empty cases \citep{V3-02757}. Ranking quality, keyword-to-query precision and query round-trip coverage are distinct outcomes. They do not establish human task success or comprehension, even when embedded in an implemented exploration workflow.

additions.context_text: Reproducibility in the extension also depends on preserving configuration and the assessed implementation. KinGVisher permits sharing graph configurations and reports code and demonstration addresses; its maximum-edge setting and property selection affect what the shared view contains. The schema library reports cached JSON schema descriptions and a schema-library repository, while SPARQL-QBE loads RDF text files into a custom browser-side executor \citep{V3-01624,V3-00138,V3-02185}. Reusing a graph image, a schema diagram or a generated query alone can therefore omit the bounds, data snapshot or executor subset needed to reproduce the result. additions.context_text: Schema-derived entry patterns also have a distinct operational contract. The peer-reviewed ShEx2SPARQL report accepts a Shape Expressions schema, an output query type and optionally a resource URI, and generates SELECT or CONSTRUCT patterns for exploring shape-conforming resources. ASK supplies an exact compliance check and requires a URI; that capability alone does not establish exploration \citep{V3-02495}. Its prototype executes 292 Wikidata Entity-Schema CONSTRUCT queries: 187 initially receive HTTP 200, and 47 more succeed with a one-result limit. Fifty-six of the 234 successful responses are empty. Request success, nonempty answers and user usefulness are therefore separate outcomes. Recursive shapes and imports remain unsupported, and no graphical authoring or recruited-user trial is established.

additions.context_text: The Hippalus automatic-ranking extension makes relaxation and ordering inspectable. SmartFSRank retains preference buckets, fills a short result set with approximate objects and uses discrimination statistics to break large ranking ties; its object explanations expose the score components and satisfied preferences. Added objects can violate hard constraints, so their approximate status affects the interpretation of the result population \citep{V3-01079}. Computational simulations use each of 382 hotels as a target: at top-one retrieval, common-value ranking requires a mean 4.11 hard constraints, compared with 4.55 without automatic ranking, while rare-value ranking worsens this to 4.85. These are simulated target-finding costs. The separately reported action latency rises from about 2 to 20 milliseconds with ranking; neither result establishes a measured human-task improvement or a performance bound for much larger data.

source_value.text: Hippalus combines iterative categorical, numeric and hierarchical facet constraints with explicit best/worst/preferTo preferences. New controls set desired result count R, maximum ranking-bucket size MB, inner-bucket ordering and preference for common or rare values. An object-level explain button reveals score components and satisfied preferences.

SmartFSRank preserves preference buckets, fills a short focus with approximately matching objects scored against hard constraints (including taxonomy-based Jaccard similarity), and breaks large ranking ties using contextual/global discrimination statistics. The interface distinguishes ranked buckets and shows per-object/per-facet score explanations; approximate results can violate hard constraints.

In its time-oriented organizational example, subject and object capsules span occurrence-to-cessation intervals and relationship arcs show activity across those intervals; current and past attributes have distinct marks \citep{V3-01484}. This is a proposed representation and visual inferencing procedure over typed semantic relationships, without an established implemented interface, RDF serialization or graph-store backend. Its authored employee-selection example motivates cognitive-fit and load hypotheses, but supplies no participant trial or cognitive-load measurement. It therefore extends the representation comparison while leaving its usability benefit open.
